Anyone interested in what wins or loses a pivotal battle should grab this primer. Not only does it detail the minute by minute decisions of those fateful days in June 1942, but it also gives an in-depth analysis of Japanese and American naval doctrine, the myriad personalities and how they shaped decision making before/during the battle, and a comprehensive look at the major differences in both sides approach to warfare in general. I've read this book about 4 times and each time I find something new to ponder or a tiny scrap of information that sparks a Google quest for additional information. Can't recommend it enough if you are interested in scholarly military history.
Shattered Sword - A Comprehensive Look at the Pivotal Battle of Midway

1. Breaking the Japanese military code gave the U.S. a fat advantage.

  2. Miracle at Midway (1983, Prange, Goldstein, Dillon) gave multiple reasons beyond #1 for USN's success: reliance on the aircraft carrier (with BBs as the backup); use of radar (the only radar using JPN ships were diverted to the Aleutians); Midway, the unsinkable carrier; the JPN force was divided in destroying the remnant US fleet and invading/occupying Midway; four out of JPN's six capital carriers were destroyed; etc.

  3. Other strategic applications were used; Prange touched on Nimitz's "formula for victory": O^2 S^4 MEC (or O2S4MEC).

I was also fascinated by the in-depth breakdown of American vs Japanese damage control philosophy and strategy, as well as the differences in carrier design and construction. It was impressive to read about why Akagi was lost to a single bomb hit and why Yorktown was able to absorb much more significant damage before being sunk.
